title: EV Charger Guide: How UK Off-Peak Tariffs Make Certain Charger Types More Profitable Than Others
content:
EV Charger Guide: How UK Off-Peak Tariffs Make Certain Charger Types More Profitable Than Others

Picking an ev charger in the UK means looking beyond the fastest model in a brochure. For most British drivers, your electricity tariff determines whether the charger becomes a genuine money-saver or an expensive regret. We find that buyers obsess over kilowatt ratings while ignoring how charger type interacts with off-peak pricing. This guide explains that relationship, and why manufacturers keep quiet about it.

Why EV Charger Type Matters More Than Speed When You Have Off-Peak Electricity

Manufacturers push charging speed harder than any other spec. Yet for typical UK home users, it's arguably irrelevant. Most drivers arrive home, plug in, and have eight or more hours before needing the car again. A 7.4 kW ev charger can typically fully replenish a 60 kWh battery overnight.

Anything faster delivers no real benefit.

What actually saves money is whether your charger can run only during off-peak hours. Smart chargers approved under OZEV funding rules must include scheduling and load-management features. The government built this in deliberately. A slower smart unit charged entirely on cheap electricity beats a faster dumb charger pulling peak-rate power every single time.

Over five years of ownership, that gap may exceed approximately £1,000 in pure electricity costs.

Home EV Chargers vs. Faster Alternatives: The Hidden Cost of Ignoring Your Tariff

An ev home charger at 7.4 kW generally costs most UK households far less per mile than a rapid public charger rated 50 kW or higher. The math is simple. Off-peak rates on Octopus Go or British Gas Electric Driver drop below 7p per kWh. Public rapid chargers bill 65p–85p per kWh.

Charging a 60 kWh battery at home on off-peak costs roughly £4.20. The same charge at a rapid charger typically costs upward of £42. The speed advantage becomes meaningless when the cost is ten times higher.

Three-phase 22 kW home chargers tend to attract enthusiasts wanting faster top-ups. According to industry guidance, most UK homes have single-phase supplies, so 22 kW installation typically needs costly grid work. More importantly, a 22 kW charger typically drains a 60 kWh battery in under three hours. It frequently finishes charging well before the off-peak window ends, generally offering no tariff advantage over standard 7.4 kW equipment.

The slower charger, used within a proper tariff schedule, is the financially smarter choice for the vast majority of UK drivers.

Installing an EV Home Charger on an Off-Peak Rate Plan—What Manufacturers Won't Tell You

Ev charger installation in the UK must follow Building Regulations Approved Document S (England) and equivalent rules across Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland. BS 7671 Section 722 typically sets out wiring standards for all electric vehicle charging points. Approved Document S requires that chargepoints in new homes and certain existing buildings be smart-enabled and able to receive load signals. This regulation exists to support off-peak demand management, yet most manufacturer brochures treat it as mere paperwork instead of a genuine financial tool.

The OZEV EV chargepoint grant covers up to £350 (verify at GOV.UK) toward purchase and installation of an approved smart home charger for eligible renters and flat owners. Approved chargers must include scheduling and meet OZEV's smart standards. The part manufacturers skip over is that chargers with more granular scheduling controls, ones allowing sub-hourly time adjustments, give owners much better ability to chase cheaper rate windows. When comparing models, ask specifically whether the app supports custom time-window scheduling, not just simple overnight delays.

Charger for EV Selection: Matching Your Electric Vehicle Charger to Economy 7 and Economy 10 Plans

Economy 7 gives seven hours of cheap electricity, usually midnight to 7 am. Economy 10 spreads ten off-peak hours across three separate windows each day. Choosing the right charger for ev use on these tariffs means understanding how each plan's structure suits your battery size. On Economy 7, a 7.4 kW charger can deliver approximately 51.8 kWh during those seven hours, enough for almost any current electric vehicle ev charger session.

On Economy 10, the split windows require your charger to support multiple scheduled sessions or continuous operation that pauses and resumes on its own.

Not all smart chargers handle Economy 10's split windows well. Some support only one scheduled session per 24 hours, meaning they can't use all three off-peak windows without manual switching. Before buying, check that the app or built-in scheduler supports at least two independent daily time windows. Drivers who can also find EV charging points near you for daytime top-ups gain extra flexibility, reducing reliance on costly peak-rate home charging when plans change.

Matching your tariff structure to charger capability is the single most important decision most UK EV owners never deliberately make.

FAQs: EV Car Charger Choices and Off-Peak Savings

Does the type of ev car charger I buy affect how much I save on off-peak tariffs?

Yes, quite a lot. Smart chargers with flexible scheduling let you confine charging to cheap-rate hours, while basic units charge immediately on plug-in regardless of timing. Over a typical year, a scheduled smart ev car charger on an off-peak tariff may save most UK drivers approximately £300–£600 compared to unscheduled charging at standard rates.

Is a faster ev charger always better for UK home use?

Not usually. If your car sits parked overnight, a 7.4 kW unit can fully charge nearly any current EV within Economy 7's seven-hour window. Faster chargers finish sooner but offer no cost advantage. They may actually cost more if the session ends early and your vehicle draws trickle power at peak rates afterward.

What should I check before ev charger installation to maximise off-peak savings?

Confirm your charger is OZEV-approved and supports your tariff's specific scheduling format, single window for Economy 7, multiple windows for Economy 10. Also check your home's single-phase supply capacity, since most UK properties support 7.4 kW without upgrades. Using a certified OZEV-registered electrician for ev charger installation generally helps ensure you meet BS 7671 and Approved Document S standards.

Can I use the OZEV grant even if I already have a tariff with off-peak rates?

Yes. The OZEV EV chargepoint grant, up to £350 (verify at GOV.UK), applies to eligible renters and flat owners on any electricity tariff. The charger must be on the OZEV-approved product list. Switching to an off-peak tariff at the same time you install maximises your financial benefit from day one.

Bottom Line

The most profitable ev charger for UK drivers is rarely the fastest. It's the one designed to work precisely within your off-peak tariff windows. Smart scheduling capability, OZEV approval, and compatibility with Economy 7 or Economy 10 deliver far larger long-term savings than an extra kilowatt of charging speed. Buy for tariff compatibility first, speed second.
